content.title: About
content.content: Toasted French or Vienna bread is a crisp slice of either whole‑grain or white loaf, achieved by a short high‑heat treatment. It features a golden crust, a characteristic aroma of caramelised starches, and a light sweetness while retaining a soft interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: French baguettes and Viennese loaves undergo longer fermentation, giving them a more pronounced flavor.
Toasted bread is traditionally used in Europe as a base for open‑face sandwiches, crostini, and soup croutons.
Toasting enhances aromatic compounds such as 2‑acetyl‑1‑pyrroline and caramelised sugars.
In many countries toasted bread with butter and garlic is served as “bruschetta”.
The crunchy crust forms through the Maillard reaction, which occurs above 150 °C.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Bread provides a steady release of energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, riboflavin and niacin in bread support metabolic processes.

items.title: Rich in fiber (especially whole‑grain versions)
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium and phosphorus in bread contribute to blood health and bone strength.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Toasted bread contains virtually no fat unless butter or spreads are added.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid traditional wheat bread.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Toasting can slightly raise the glycemic index, which is relevant for diabetics.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Some breads contain added salt and preservatives; choose additive‑free options when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted bread works well for sandwiches, as a base for pâtés, avocado, cheese, or as soup croutons. Sprinkle with herbs, garlic butter, or grated cheese and finish under the broiler for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep toasted bread in a dry container or paper bag at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze slices in a sealed bag and re‑toast in a toaster before serving.
